subject.title: Feature: Distinguish webchat client types (Mac app vs browser)

question: Which WebChat client metadata, if any, should OpenClaw expose to agents: a coarse validated client class, detailed connect-frame fields, or no model-visible client identity?
rationale: Current protocol already carries client identity, but making it model-visible changes the prompt and trust boundary; raw headers and browser hints are spoofable while native/connect metadata still needs a product contract.

options.title: Expose Coarse Validated Class
options.body: Map known connect-frame ids and modes to a bounded runtime field such as `client=macos-app` or `client=browser-webchat`, and keep raw headers/User-Agent out of agent context.

options.title: Keep Identity Diagnostic-Only
options.body: Continue using client identity in gateway logs and debugging surfaces while leaving the agent runtime prompt at `channel=webchat`.

options.title: Expose Untrusted Hints Explicitly
options.body: Allow client-supplied hints for debugging but label and sanitize them as untrusted so agents and plugins do not treat them as authorization or capability facts.

recommendation.title: Expose Coarse Validated Class
recommendation.body: Map known connect-frame ids and modes to a bounded runtime field such as `client=macos-app` or `client=browser-webchat`, and keep raw headers/User-Agent out of agent context.

likelyOwner.reason: Their gateway chat/provenance and runtime-channel history is closest to the model-visible context decision this issue needs.
